title: Meet the tones
description: Learn what tone marks mean before building your first phrases.
objectives: Recognize the four written tone marks.
Notice that tones change in connected speech.
explanation: In Mandarin, pitch patterns help distinguish words. Pinyin marks the four tones: mā (high and level), má (rising), mǎ (low, with a possible rise), and mà (falling). These are a guide to pitch, not four different volume levels.
A third tone is often low without a full dip and rise inside a phrase. When two third tones meet, the first is usually pronounced like a second tone: 你好 is written nǐ hǎo but commonly spoken ní hǎo.
A neutral-tone syllable is short and unstressed; its pitch depends on the preceding tone. These questions check tone concepts. They do not measure your spoken pronunciation or acoustic tone accuracy.

examples.meaning: Mum — first tone: high and level.
Water — third tone; its shape depends on context.
Mum — the second syllable is neutral in this common pronunciation.

questions.prompt: Written-tone check: which tone is high and level?
questions.explanation: The first tone is high and level. The mark ā is a reminder of a level pitch.
questions.hint: Look for the horizontal tone mark.

questions.prompt: Written-tone check: the mark in chá represents which pattern?
questions.explanation: The acute mark á represents the second, rising tone.

questions.prompt: Written-tone check: which syllable has a fourth tone?
questions.explanation: The mark ì slopes downward and denotes the fourth tone.

questions.prompt: In ordinary speech, how is the first tone of nǐ hǎo usually pronounced?
questions.explanation: Before another third tone, the first third tone normally changes to a rising second tone. Dictionary pinyin still writes nǐ hǎo.
questions.hint: This phrase places two third tones together.

questions.prompt: Which description fits a neutral-tone syllable?

options.text: Short and unstressed; pitch depends on context

questions.explanation: Neutral tone is not a fixed fifth pitch contour. It is unstressed and changes with context.
questions.hint: Think of the second syllable in māma.

title: First connections
description: Say hello, thank someone, and turn a statement into a question.
objectives: Understand common greetings.
Use 吗 at the end of a yes-or-no question.
explanation: 你好 (nǐ hǎo) is a useful beginner greeting. 谢谢 (xièxie) means “thank you”, and 不客气 (bú kèqi) is a common reply meaning “you are welcome”. Use 再见 (zàijiàn) to say goodbye.
Add 吗 (ma) at the end of a statement to make a yes-or-no question. 你好吗？ asks “How are you?” literally “Are you well?”; it is a useful learning example, not the only natural way to greet someone.
Pinyin below usually shows dictionary tones. Some examples show the spoken form: 不 is normally pronounced bú before a fourth tone, as in 不客气. Do not judge every syllable in isolation.

examples.meaning: You are welcome. (Spoken tone change on 不.)
How are you? / Are you well?

questions.prompt: Play the example and choose its meaning.
questions.explanation: 你好 is the greeting “hello”. Its first syllable changes tone before the second third tone.
questions.hint: The two characters literally relate to “you” and “good”.

questions.prompt: Someone says 谢谢. Which reply means “you are welcome”?
questions.explanation: 不客气 is a common reply to 谢谢.
questions.hint: Choose the expression that tells someone there is no need to be polite.

questions.prompt: Build: “Are you well?”
questions.explanation: The statement 你好 becomes a yes-or-no question when 吗 is added at the end.

questions.prompt: Where does 吗 go in this kind of yes-or-no question?
questions.explanation: 吗 follows the whole statement. The original word order stays the same.

questions.prompt: Choose the expression for “goodbye”.
questions.explanation: 再见 means “goodbye”, literally suggesting seeing someone again.
questions.hint: It is the expression used when leaving.

fact.title: A very old writing tradition
fact.text: Shang rulers recorded questions and outcomes on animal bones and tortoiseshells. These oracle-bone inscriptions preserve early Chinese written records, including questions about rain and hunting.
fact.sourceLabel: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art

title: This is me
description: Introduce yourself and build your first complete statements.
objectives: Introduce your name and identity.
Place a time expression before the action.
explanation: 我 means “I” and 你 means “you”. Use 叫 for a name: 我叫安娜 means “My name is Anna”. Use 是 before a noun describing an identity: 我是学生 means “I am a student”.
你叫什么名字？ asks “What is your name?” Here 什么 already asks “what”, so do not add 吗. 安娜 is an example name, not a required translation of your own name.
A basic action sentence follows subject → verb → object: 我学习汉语. A time expression such as 今天 goes before the verb, either before or after the subject: 今天我学习汉语 / 我今天学习汉语.

questions.prompt: Play the sentence and choose what the speaker tells you.
questions.explanation: 我叫安娜 introduces the speaker’s name: Anna.

questions.prompt: Build: “I am a student.”
questions.explanation: 是 links the subject 我 to the noun 学生.

questions.prompt: Which word introduces your name in 我___安娜？
questions.explanation: 叫 introduces what a person is called. 是 is used for identity, not in this name pattern.

questions.prompt: Build: “I study Chinese today.”
questions.explanation: 今天 goes before 学习. It can appear before or after 我, so both time placements are accepted.
questions.hint: Keep 今天 before the action.

questions.prompt: Why does 你叫什么名字？ not need 吗?
questions.explanation: 吗 creates a yes-or-no question; 什么 already asks for the missing information.
questions.hint: What kind of answer does “what is your name?” request?

title: People around me
description: Talk about family, possession, and things people like.
objectives: Use 的 for a possessive phrase.
Say who someone is and what they like.
explanation: 爸爸 means “dad” and 妈妈 means “mum”. 我的妈妈 means “my mum”: the owner comes first, then 的, then the person or thing. With close family, 的 is also often omitted, as in 我妈妈.
他 and 她 are written differently but both are pronounced tā. 是 introduces an identity, while 有 means “have”. When counting people, 一个 is a basic number-classifier combination.
喜欢 means “like”. Put 也, meaning “also”, before the verb: 妈妈也喜欢茶. A neutral second syllable in bàba or māma should not be treated as a full fourth or first tone.

examples.meaning: I have one daughter. (A common spoken form of 一个.)

questions.prompt: Play the phrase and choose the family member.
questions.explanation: 妈妈 is mum. Its second syllable is commonly neutral.

questions.prompt: Build the full possessive phrase: “my mum”. Use every tile.
questions.explanation: In the full possessive form, the owner 我 comes before 的 and 妈妈. 我妈妈 is also natural, but this exercise supplies 的.

questions.prompt: Build: “She is a teacher.”
questions.explanation: 她 is the subject, 是 links the identity, and 老师 is teacher.

questions.prompt: Where does 也 go in “Mum also likes tea”?
questions.explanation: The pattern is 妈妈也喜欢茶: 也 comes before the verb 喜欢.

questions.prompt: Build: “I like tea, and Dad likes tea too.”
questions.explanation: Each clause has a subject and 喜欢茶. The second clause adds 也 before 喜欢. Identical 茶 and 喜欢 tiles are interchangeable.
questions.hint: Finish 我喜欢茶 first, then add the clause about Dad.

title: Tea, please
description: Ask for a drink and describe what you do or do not drink.
objectives: Build subject–verb–object sentences.
Use 想 and 不 before the action.
Recognize a quantity phrase for a drink.
explanation: 喝 means “drink”. Start with the subject, then the verb, then the drink: 我喝水. 想 before the verb expresses wanting to do something: 我想喝茶 means “I would like to drink tea”.
不 goes before the verb to negate a habitual action or present intention: 我不喝茶 means “I do not drink tea”. Here 不 is bù because 喝 has a first tone; before a fourth tone it normally changes to bú.

For a drink, 一杯水 means “one cup of water”: number → container measure → drink. 杯子 is the noun “cup”; 杯 is the measure used in this phrase. 一 has dictionary tone yī but is pronounced yì before the first tone of 杯.

examples.meaning: I would like to drink tea.
One cup of water, thank you.

questions.prompt: Play the sentence. What does the speaker want to drink?
questions.explanation: 我想喝茶 ends in 茶: the speaker wants tea.

questions.prompt: Build: “I drink water.”
questions.explanation: The subject 我 comes before 喝, and the object 水 follows it.

questions.prompt: Build: “I would like to drink tea.”
questions.explanation: 想 goes before the action 喝: wanting to drink tea.
questions.hint: Place 想 immediately before 喝.

questions.prompt: What does 我不喝茶 mean?
questions.explanation: 不 negates 喝, while 茶 remains the object.

questions.prompt: Build: “one cup of water”.
questions.explanation: Put the number first, then 杯 as the container measure, then the drink 水.

fact.title: Tea is also a social practice
fact.text: In 2022, UNESCO listed China’s traditional tea processing and associated social practices as intangible cultural heritage. The entry includes drinking and sharing tea, not only producing it.

title: First journey checkpoint
description: Bring greetings, family, drinks, and sentence patterns together.
objectives: Choose expressions that fit a short encounter.
Recall tone changes and basic sentence patterns without hints.
explanation: This stop reviews the first unit. Aim to answer at least 80% independently; hints remain available for learning but assisted answers do not raise the independent score.

Listen to an example when the speaker button is available. This review checks understanding and sentence construction. It does not certify spoken tone accuracy; use the linked speaking practice to rehearse and compare recordings.

questions.prompt: Play the sentence and choose the correct meaning.
questions.explanation: 妈妈 is mum; 喜欢 is like; 茶 is tea.
questions.hint: Identify the subject and the drink separately.

questions.prompt: Build: “I am a student.”
questions.explanation: Identity uses subject → 是 → noun.
questions.hint: 是 connects a person to an identity.

questions.prompt: Which statement about spoken 你好 is correct?

options.text: Both syllables must always have a full dip and rise
The first syllable is always neutral
The first third tone usually becomes rising before the next third tone

questions.explanation: Third-tone sandhi changes the first tone to a rising tone in this two-syllable phrase.
questions.hint: Recall what happens when two third tones meet.

questions.prompt: Build: “I would like to drink water.”
questions.explanation: 想 precedes 喝, and 水 follows the action as its object.

questions.prompt: Build: “I study Chinese today.”
questions.explanation: The time expression 今天 goes before 学习, either before or after 我.

title: Meet a new classmate
description: Listen, choose a reply, and introduce yourself in a short encounter.
objectives: Understand a simple introduction.
Choose a suitable response.
Construct statements and questions.
explanation: You meet Anna before a Chinese class. Complete the five tasks in the conversation. Everything needed is shown in the examples, and you can enter this exercise without completing the course.
Use 叫 for names, 是 for identities, and 吗 for a yes-or-no question. The answers in this activity check comprehension and sentence order, not your spoken pronunciation.

questions.prompt: Listen to Anna. What does she tell you?
questions.explanation: 叫 introduces a name; 安娜 is Anna.
questions.hint: Focus on the words after 叫.

questions.prompt: You want to greet Anna back. Which expression fits?
questions.explanation: 你好 is the greeting. 再见 would end the encounter.
questions.hint: Choose the greeting, not the farewell.

questions.prompt: Build: “My name is Anna.”
questions.explanation: The pattern 我叫 + name introduces the speaker.

questions.prompt: Build: “I am a student.”
questions.explanation: 是 connects 我 to the identity 学生.
questions.hint: Use the identity verb between the person and noun.

questions.prompt: Ask: “Are you a teacher?”
questions.explanation: Start with 你是老师, then add 吗 to make a yes-or-no question.

title: A family portrait
description: Understand who someone is and describe the people around them.
objectives: Understand a family description.
Use possession and identity.
Connect two preferences using 也.
explanation: Imagine showing a family photo to a friend. Identify the person, explain their job, and compare what people like. Listen where an audio example is provided, then build your own sentences.
我的妈妈 is the full possessive form of “my mum”; 我妈妈 is also common. 也 goes before the verb, not at the end of the sentence.

questions.prompt: Listen. What is the speaker’s mum’s job?
questions.explanation: 老师 is teacher. The sentence says 我的妈妈是老师.

questions.prompt: Build the full phrase “my mum” using every tile.
questions.explanation: The full possessive form puts 的 between the owner and the person.

questions.prompt: Build: “She is a teacher.”
questions.explanation: The identity pattern is subject → 是 → job.
questions.hint: Use 是 to connect the two nouns.

questions.prompt: 爸爸也喜欢茶 tells you that…
questions.explanation: 也 means “also” and 喜欢茶 means “like tea”.
questions.hint: Look at what 也 adds to the meaning.

questions.prompt: Build: “I like tea, and Dad likes tea too.”
questions.explanation: Build the first statement, then put 也 before 喜欢 in the second. Identical word tiles can exchange places.
questions.hint: Keep the comma between the two clauses.

title: A stop at the café
description: Choose a drink, order it, and finish the exchange politely.
objectives: Understand a drink choice.
Express what you want and do not want.
Use a quantity phrase and a polite ending.
explanation: You stop for a drink with a friend. Understand their choice, say what you would like, and order a cup of water. This is a short guided scenario rather than an unrestricted conversation simulator.
想 precedes the action, 不 negates it, and a quantity phrase follows number → measure → drink. 一杯水，谢谢 is a concise order: “One cup of water, thank you.”

examples.meaning: I would like to drink tea.
One cup of water, thank you.

questions.prompt: Listen to your friend. Which drink do they want?
questions.explanation: 茶 is the final word in 我想喝茶: your friend wants tea.

questions.prompt: Build: “I would like to drink water.”
questions.explanation: 想 precedes 喝 and 水 is the object of the action.

questions.prompt: Build: “I do not drink tea.”
questions.explanation: Place 不 directly before 喝 to negate the action.
questions.hint: The negative word goes before the verb.

questions.prompt: Build: “One cup of water, thank you.”
questions.explanation: 一杯水 is the quantity phrase; 谢谢 adds a polite ending.
questions.hint: Finish the order before the comma.

questions.prompt: The server says 不客气 after your 谢谢. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 不客气 is a common reply to thanks.
questions.hint: Recall the exchange from the greetings stop.
